security_spec.violation_condition: In bhyve vmmops_run() at sys/riscv/vmm/vmm_riscv.c:632, csr_write(henvcfg, HENVCFG_STCE) unconditionally clears all other henvcfg fields including CBZE, CBCFE, and CBIE without save/restore across vCPU context switch. The spec now mandates that henvcfg.CBIE overrides guest senvcfg.CBIE semantics (flush vs invalidate cascade), so any future CBO passthrough without proper henvcfg save/restore leaks CBIE override state between vCPUs, or conversely, a missing restore of zeroed CBO bits causes guest-expected CBO.INVAL invalidate semantics to be silently downgraded to flush—corrupting guest cache-coherency invariants.
security_spec.summary: bhyve writes henvcfg without save/restore; spec PR adds explicit CBIE cascade (henvcfg overrides guest senvcfg invalidate→flush), making any CBO passthrough without proper context-switch virtualization a cross-vCPU CBIE state leak and guest data corruption vector

findings.finding: csr_write(henvcfg, HENVCFG_STCE) unconditionally clears all other henvcfg fields (CBZE, CBCFE, CBIE, PBMTE, FIOM) on every vCPU run entry. henvcfg is not saved/restored across vCPU context switches — it is absent from both vmmops_vcpu_save_csrs() and vmmops_vcpu_restore_csrs(), and the hypcsr structure has no henvcfg field. The RISC-V spec states henvcfg.CBIE overrides guest senvcfg.CBIE semantics (flush vs invalidate cascade), so any future CBO passthrough that sets CBZE/CBCFE/CBIE would have those bits silently cleared on every vCPU entry, downgrading guest-expected CBO.INVAL invalidate to flush semantics and corrupting guest cache-coherency invariants. Currently no immediate data-corruption because CBO passthrough is not yet implemented, but the architectural gap is a latent vulnerability.
